key_decisions.note: Hebrew peloni almoni deliberately withholds the nearer redeemer's name. TSW 'friend' is smoother but loses the literary anonymity. Fluent preserves the anonymity explicitly.

key_decisions.decision: preserve redeem / redeemer / redemption lexical network
key_decisions.note: This network structures the chapter and should not be varied for elegance.
Retains the legal transaction language without replacing it with explanatory modern concepts. Apparatus should provide cultural/legal context.
Naturalizes 'manner of attestation' while preserving legal function.

key_decisions.decision: prosper in Ephrathah and make a name for yourself in Bethlehem
key_decisions.note: Natural English for the blessing while preserving house/name vocabulary.
Natural contemporary English for the Hebrew sexual euphemism 'went in to her'; no added detail.

key_decisions.decision: the LORD enabled her to conceive
key_decisions.note: Naturalizes 'gave her conception' while preserving explicit divine agency.
Preserves shuv-nephesh and echoes the book's larger return/restoration pattern.
Hebrew omeneth can denote a nurse/caretaker/foster role. 'Caregiver' avoids implying wet-nursing without evidence.

key_decisions.decision: He became the father of Jesse, the father of David
key_decisions.note: Makes genealogical relation natural without changing sequence.

book_level_findings: ḥesed should remain steadfast love in Ruth 1:8, 2:20, and 3:10.
go'el / ga'al / ge'ullah should remain visibly connected through redeemer / redeem / redemption.
rest language in Ruth 1:9 and 3:1/18 should remain a thematic network.
empty / empty-handed / restoration should remain visible across 1:21, 3:17, and 4:15.
Boaz as a man of standing (2:1) and Ruth as a woman of standing (3:11) should remain lexically paired.
